Rules / Tool

SK9017 An option was set to a value outside its domain

A key Skala owns was set, on a line the author wrote, to a value the option does not accept. The value was discarded, and the message names the reason and what is in force instead. ⚠ Warning, yet it fails skala config check on its own: it is the one warning that fails the command without --strict, and the only diagnostic that exits it with 3 (configuration error) rather than 1. Correct the value or delete the line.

CategoryTool
Default severitywarning
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

SK9001 is info because the export carries some two thousand keys Skala will never implement and the user wrote nothing wrong. This is the opposite case: the key is in the registry, Skala owns it, the intent was recorded and then thrown away, and the code is formatted against a value nobody chose — for skala_keep_existing_declaration_block_arrangement that is the arranger rearranging a file on the strength of a setting it discarded. Non-negotiable #4 (docs/plan/00) says unknown configuration is a diagnostic and never a silent default; these were computed and reported to nobody until M9. It exits 3 rather than waiting for --strict because every other warning describes a configuration that means something and might mean the wrong thing, and this one describes a line that means nothing at all. config explain marks the row (default) ⚠ SK9017 file:line.

Example

Instead of:

skala_max_line_length = -1
skala_accessor_owner_body = sideways

Write:

skala_max_line_length = 120
skala_accessor_owner_body = expression_body

When it does not fire

indent_size = tab is not reported: the EditorConfig specification defines it as tab_width's value and Skala substitutes it before validating, though a bad tab_width is its own finding. Only keys the author typed are checked — a value a generalised key propagates into a target whose domain rejects it is dropped silently, because they never wrote the target's name. An unknown --option on the command line is SK9001, not this. Error-severity configuration diagnostics (SK9003, SK9007, SK9012, and SK9008 under the default drift policy) also fail check without --strict, at exit 1; this is the only warning that does.
